# sk-cbor acceptance check

The pinned source at `f3ee26dd824205a760aadba8199aa93d6d7d0d8a` was checked offline with Rust 1.99.0. The crate version label is 0.1.2, but the subject is the pinned source snapshot. The result is 19 surviving mutants in sk-cbor’s own unit and doc tests from 100 runtime mutants, and no reproduced normative wire deviation in the declared subset.

[Surviving mutants and dispositions](acceptance/MISSING-TESTS.md) gives each green codec-suite run, its red package probe, and its upstream disposition. [The patch](acceptance/upstream-tests.patch) applies to the pinned checkout. It is the exact `git diff 79e85b9..f6666ff` and adds 10 boundary, depth and ordering tests. Append (M033) is evidenced by existing downstream tests; duplicate-key strictness (M099) is not proposed upstream. [The deferred patch](acceptance/deferred-tests.patch) keeps four consolidated conversion and vector tests in the package. [Findings](acceptance/FINDINGS.md) gives the conformance classifications and documentation limits.

The package’s own files are licensed under **Apache-2.0 OR MIT**; see [LICENSE-APACHE](LICENSE-APACHE) and [LICENSE-MIT](LICENSE-MIT). Third-party files, including OpenSK sources, RFC texts and test vectors, retain their own licences.

[Upstream review](acceptance/UPSTREAM-REVIEW.md) records the final commit, debug/release replay, exact counts and the supplied 2026-10-13 upstream checkpoint. [PR text](acceptance/UPSTREAM-PR.md) includes provenance. The separate [documentation patch](acceptance/upstream-doc.patch) corrects the construction-panic contract and the write_nested error link without changing code.

| Item | Class | Result |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | DOCUMENTED | Negative major-type-1 values below i64::MIN are outside the model. |
| F2 | DOCUMENTED | Floats and simple values other than false, true, null and undefined return public unsupported-value errors. |
| F3 | DOCUMENTED | Default depth is 127; optional nesting limits are supported. |
| F4 | DOCUMENTED | Duplicate construction keys panic; tag values remain structural. |
| F5 | AMBIGUOUS | Decoder canonical-only restrictions are implemented, but not stated explicitly in the reader docs. |
| F6 | AMBIGUOUS | README uses “canonical order” without naming the profile; code resolves it to RFC 8949 bytewise order. |
| F7 | DOC MISMATCH | cbor_map_options docs promise writing failure for duplicates, but construction panics; write_nested docs link DecoderError instead of EncoderError; no normative wire deviation. |
| F8 | KNOWN | #788 string-length hardening is present; native and simulated-width tests reject announced 2^32-byte strings. |

No reproduced DEVIATION from a normative requirement in the declared codec slice was found. AMBIGUOUS means the documented applicability or contract is incomplete; it does not assert that a normative clause permits two key orders under the same selected profile.
Existing nesting coverage includes `test_read_too_much_nesting_error` through private Reader methods, and `test_write_single_levels`, `test_write_nested_map_levels`, `test_write_unbalanced_nested_containers` and `test_write_overly_nested` through private Writer methods. `test_write_nested_map_levels` and `test_write_overly_nested` also assert that `None` succeeds. The remaining gaps are the public `read`/`write` wrappers’ default constant (127), the `None` pass-through of `read_nested`/`write_nested`, and the tag branch’s nesting budget.

`None` disables nesting checks by documented intent: [OpenSK PR #373](https://github.com/google/OpenSK/pull/373), merged 2021-09-09, explicitly preserves `{read,write}_nested(..., None)` for users who want to skip nesting checks. The supplied body excerpt is retained in the final receipt. Tests at 128 arrays are bounded evidence for that intent; they do not establish resource safety for arbitrary depth.

Tag accounting is the one open contract question: the tests pin one level; maintainers are asked to confirm or reject it.

`libraries/cbor/examples/cbor.rs` is an asserting program that `cargo test` builds but does not run; run by the review, it detects none of the 19 survivors.

The writer follows RFC 8949 §4.2.1 bytewise key order. The README only says “canonical order”. CTAP 2.1 §8 uses major-type-first scalar-key order; it is not the global length-first order in RFC 7049 §3.9. Arrays, maps and tags are also ordered by their deterministic encoded bytes, but are outside CTAP’s scalar-key note.

The supplied cbor/test-vectors corpus derives from RFC 7049 Appendix A and uses 44 of 82 vectors in the acceptance and deferred tests. The 38 nonapplicable rows comprise 23 float-containing vectors, 2 unsupported simple values plus 1 legacy reserved simple encoding, 1 negative integer below i64::MIN, and 11 indefinite encodings. The 11 indefinite vectors have representable values, but their original bytes cannot be emitted by this deterministic writer. Two tagged bignums are tested structurally and their numeric meaning is checked by the independent model. The f818 simple(24) example was removed from RFC 8949 Appendix A; it is reserved/not well-formed under RFC 8949 §3.3. [Vector rows](acceptance/vectors.json) list every index and reason.

The five doc examples have no output assertions, as expected for usage examples; no change proposed. `test_read_unsigned` does not cover unsigned values above i64::MAX. `test_value_ordering` does not cover equal-prefix tails or same-tag content ordering. Other assertions in those unit tests remain useful.

Run from the workspace root:

```sh
export ACCEPTANCE_FORMAT=/path/to/acceptance-format
./run_all.sh
```

The script uses the local `.cargo-home`, local target directory, `--offline`, and `RUSTFLAGS="--cap-lints warn"`. It never fetches dependencies. Rustdoc uses `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1` only to persist the five doc-test executables on the pinned stable toolchain. The schemata library and unit tests are compiled once. Every id runs the same 78 unit tests and five saved doc binaries without invoking Cargo. Id 0 uses the original branches. Candidate tests are compiled into that same binary and excluded from the shipped-suite filter. Each mutant gets one exact red probe.

Targeted replay after a full run:

```sh
python3 acceptance/check_claim.py 1
SK_CBOR_MUTANT=1 python3 acceptance/check_claim.py 1
```

The first command is green; the second is red. A ten-second timeout counts as a detection, not a green result. M005 deliberately permits recursive decoding without progress and is detected this way.

The reference model starts from RFC wire grammar, retains structural tags, and generates preferred encodings independently of the crate. It checked 363057 unique inputs with seed 8949, including all inputs of length zero through two. Every input receives an independent acceptance/rejection check. Every accepted input receives both exact decode→encode byte comparison and a structural decoded-value comparison with the reference model (integer sign and magnitude, byte strings, Unicode scalars, arrays, map pairs, tags and simple identity). Official vector assertions also compare constructed expected values as well as bytes.

[The acceptance file](acceptance/acceptance.toml) has one row per declared rule, behaviour, public item and supplied vector. The 109 public surface rows include every crate-owned public type, function, macro, constant, explicit trait implementation and derived trait implementation, plus namespace/re-export and auto-trait accounting. 30 public rows explicitly remain gaps, including compile-time constants, derived Clone/Debug, unreachable error variants and language-level structural traits. No separate structural mutant builds are claimed for these gaps. Namespace/re-export gaps concern independent mutation, not whether names compile. Only observed-red behavioural probes carry weighted claims. [API rows](acceptance/API.md) expose all gaps. The validator entry point `check_acceptance.py` binds the verification meaning. The normative/vector projection [conformance.toml](acceptance/conformance.toml) is checked separately with the conformance meaning; it does not duplicate the whole-API rows.

The checks are bounded native tests, not a proof for every byte string. They do not execute a 32-bit target, prove allocator/stack safety under unlimited nesting, measure embedded timing, validate tag semantics in applications, or validate complete CTAP messages. #788 is checked natively and with a clearly labeled u32 truncation model. The supplied issue/PR snapshots and full CBOR history were searched by content; the record includes #788, #639, #384 and #373. No network or git commit is used.

The measured mutation/comparison run took 51.31 seconds. Its build phase has four tool invocations: one schemata build, one doc-test build (five binaries), one published-consumer test build and one bridge build. Independent PR and deferred verification adds four test builds across the two source commits. There are zero per-id rebuilds and no separately compiled mutant variants. Initial preparation included failed import/alloc compilations and an aborted timeout run; these are disclosed in the evidence, not included in the final clean-run wall time. Validator results are retained under `acceptance/evidence/gen/validate-*.txt`.

Builds use local `.cargo-home` and target directories, `--offline`, and `RUSTFLAGS="--cap-lints warn"`.
